featured_reviews.review_text: I have visited this restaurant/cafe 2-3 times before with my college friends and had no issues, though I am vegetarian by choice not religion and they were non-veg. Today I came with my best friend who is vegetarian by religion. We ordered and confirmed we wanted a veg dish which I recommend I loved because I had tried it before. After one bite my friend threw up because there were clearly chicken pieces in it. And because I am a vegetarian by my choice and not religion so I have had chicken before and I immediately got to know it was chicken pieces. I called the waiter immediately, very upset, and told him how careless and unprofessional this was. Instead of checking the dish in front of us, he took the whole bowl to the kitchen and came back after 15-20 minutes with actual veg makhani pasta, saying it was not chicken, it was just paneer. We could clearly spot the difference between the previous served dish(chicken slices) and newly prepared dish(paneer cubes) . If it was paneer he could have confirmed it on the spot instead of taking 20 minutes, which made it feel like he was trying to gaslight us and avoid a bad impression for the restaurant. If this would have happened to someone else they would have definitely crashed out but just because we did not want to spoil our own mood we let it go. If am ordering vegetarian, I must get a vegetarian dish, and for someone veg by religion this caused real distress and hurt her religious sentiments. I have attached photos and I never thought I would have to rate this restaurant 1 star.

I walked into this place expecting something legendary — the way people crowd around it, you’d think they were serving liquid gold. The vibe? Nice. The energy? Buzzing. The hype? Massive.

But then there’s me — someone who casually runs on 500mg of caffeine a day. My tolerance isn’t normal. My standards aren’t either.

So when I took that first sip… I waited. I expected fireworks. A caffeine punch. Some kind of “main character” awakening moment.
It never came.

The coffee? It’s normal. Decent. Drinkable. But not life-changing. Not the kind that makes you pause mid-sip and rethink your existence. For someone with my caffeine level, it felt pretty average.

Maybe for casual coffee drinkers, this place hits differently. But for me? It’s just another stop in the daily grind. Not bad — just not worth the hype.

I guess when you live on high caffeine settings, ordinary doesn’t impress you that easily. ☕😌
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text:
Thanks a lot Ashish for taking the time to write such a detailed (and honestly, quite entertaining) review - we genuinely appreciate it.

We truly value feedback from someone like you who clearly understands and enjoys coffee at a deeper level. It helps us look at our product from a sharper lens and keep improving.

That said, we also want to add a little perspective from our side. At Rs.35 a cup, our goal has never been to serve a "life-changing" or "firework-in-a-cup" experience - because coffee at that level usually come with a very different setup, sourcing, and pricing.

What we aim to do is keep things honest, consistent, and accessible -- a good reliable cup of coffee that people can enjoy everyday without overthinking or overspending.

We completely understand that someone running on 500mg caffeine and chasing that "main character moment' this might feel subtle or even average - and thats fair.

But we're glad you noticed the vibe and energy - because thats a big part of what we are building here. 

Appreciate you stopping by and sharing your honest thoughts. Hope to see you again soon!
